# AzureDeck 1.9.13 — Launcher choice, installed-app icons and auto-rejoin

Choose Roblox or Bloxstrap in Accounts > Launch center or Settings > Launch & recovery. Both cards show installed/missing status and use the installed executable's own icon, with a small fallback mark when unavailable. AzureDeck refreshes the local checks and checks again before saving a different choice. Missing/incomplete installs are rejected without replacing the previous choice. Both official setup links are available. Selection saves automatically and transfers with clipboard config.

Roblox uses its complete official Player installation and an account-specific launch URI; Bloxstrap keeps its managed preparation/launch flow. Public games, specific servers, private links, queued selection and Discord share the selected backend. Both use owned process jobs and matching account/place join logs. Each launcher has its own persistent installation-error state and repair budget. Switching is blocked during an active launch/queue/repair or unfinished launcher job. Native recovery uses a fresh signed Roblox installer; its owned auto-opened Home client is closed before completion. Neither backend deletes the whole data folder. Rendering overrides follow the selected launcher.

Crash and persistent-Unknown auto-rejoin are now separate global switches, enabled by default for signed-in accounts with a saved destination. Unexpected process exits schedule recovery after the configured cooldown. Unknown, unconfirmed startup, a missing/hung client window, or an actual Unknown monitoring result must persist through the Unknown grace period (default 60 seconds) before scheduling a live-client rejoin. Disabled monitoring does not itself trigger recovery. A fresh account ticket is obtained before replacing a live client.

The existing cooldown is retained (default 60 seconds). The attempt limit is per incident (default three; zero disables retries) and resets after 60 seconds of stable health. Offline waits do not consume an attempt. Healthy status before the cooldown cancels Unknown recovery. In-app stops/cancelled queue items invalidate pending recovery and cannot relaunch on the next tick. Confirmed access-denial/kick codes 267/600 retain their no-rejoin protection. Existing optional per-account disconnect-dialog recovery remains separate.

Unknown can reflect unavailable monitoring as well as a client problem; its switch and grace period control that behavior. Use Stop/queue cancellation to suppress an account until its next explicit launch. Closing a game outside AzureDeck is still treated as an unexpected exit. Status and recovery errors remain visible; repeated failure stops at the configured limit.

Executed validation includes native launcher ownership/maintenance fixtures, complete/incomplete installation checks, independent backend state, real watchdog scheduling with injected offline/launch callbacks, cancellation and UI/icon previews. No live account was joined and no real installer/update was executed during tests. See VALIDATION.md.
